exams.syllabus: ABRSM Bowed Strings Practical Grades from 2024. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: Pieces 30 each (90 total, 60%); Scales and arpeggios 21 (14%); Sight-reading 21 (14%); Aural tests 18 (12%); total 150. Pass 100–119, Merit 120–129, Distinction 130–150 (Below Pass 50–99). A pass in every component is not required to pass overall.

Three pieces, one from each of Lists A (faster, technical agility), B (lyrical, expressive) and C (varied traditions/styles); at least one must be accompanied. Live piano (or listed string) accompaniment required except for pieces marked SOLO; Initial–Grade 3 may use string accompaniment/duets (DUET or DUET/PIANO; candidate plays the upper part unless stated). Candidates bring their own accompanist (teacher may accompany; no recorded accompaniment; accompanist may simplify). Listed editions are mandatory only for arrangements/transcriptions. Da capo and dal segno must be observed; other repeats (incl. first-time bars) omitted unless very short. Cadenzas omitted unless specified; long tuttis cut; either ossia allowed. Memory optional, no extra marks. Teacher/accompanist may tune at Initial–Grade 5; candidates tune themselves at Grades 6–8. Scales, sight-reading and aural unchanged from the previous syllabus.
sections: Scales & technical work
Scales: G, D majors from open strings, 1 oct., separate bows, even notes or long tonic (candidate's choice); A minor from bottom A to a 5th, separate bows, even notes. (All three played.)
Sight-reading

4 bars (4/4) or 6 bars (2/4); time: 4/4 or 2/4; new features: 1st position; crotchet and quaver note values, crotchet rests; notes separately bowed; mf; new keys: G, D majors; range: G–c, d–g. Unaccompanied; 30 seconds to prepare; parameters are cumulative from earlier grades.
Aural & other tests
Clap the pulse; clap back rhythm echoes of two 2-bar phrases; sing back two 1-bar echoes (tonic–mediant, major); answer a question on dynamics or articulation of a piece.
Performance Grades / digital option

Performance Grades (Initial/Grade 1–8) use the same repertoire lists but consist of four pieces (three from the lists plus one own choice) and a mark for the performance as a whole, with no scales, sight-reading or aural; currently assessed by video-recorded submission. The same Grade 5 prerequisite applies for Grades 6–8 and marks cannot be transferred between the two.

Teachers may help tune up to G5; G6-8 candidates tune unaided.

Two pathways, same entry process; exam filmed as one continuous take. Technical work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance criteria 20 = 100. Technical work played as one unit in listed order (before, after or between pieces); bowed strings play the bowing exercise (not at Initial) then EITHER one fixed set of scales/arpeggios/technical exercises (set A or set B - every item in the set is played, with bowings specified, from memory) OR two studies (G1-5) / two orchestral extracts from different groups (G6-8), candidate's choice; harp plays the listed scales/arpeggios/exercises OR two studies OR (pedal harp G6-8) two orchestral extracts. Backing tracks/recorded accompaniment allowed at all grades in digital exams.
sections: Technical work

1) Bowing: set rhythm per note (dotted crotchet = 50). EITHER 2) A, Bb, Eb major and C, G minor (harmonic or melodic) 2 oct (scales separate or two beats per bow; arpeggios separate or slurred three); dominant 7ths in F (from open C) and G (from D on C string) 2 oct and in Eb (from Bb) 1 oct, separate or slurred in pairs; chromatic from open G 1 oct, separate. Min: scales 69, arpeggios dotted crotchet 44, 7ths 69. Technical exercise: octaves and sixths from open G, D, C (crotchet = 100). OR 3) Studies (music allowed): prepare all three, candidate plays one, examiner picks one of the other two: Lament, Countdown, Barcarolle.
Supporting tests

Choose 2 of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge. Sight reading (30s prep, about two grades below the exam; cumulative): adds dotted crotchets, quaver rests; cresc./decresc.; slurs up to 4 notes, accents, staccato, pizzicato, forward extensions; keys A major; E, B minor; accidentals. Aural: 4-bar harmonised piece in 4 or 6 time - clap pulse; major/minor; final cadence perfect or imperfect; interval quality (minor/major 2nd, 3rd, 6th; perfect 4th/5th); with a copy, find the bars of a rhythm change and a pitch change. Improvisation: stylistic - 12 bars over piano (adagio or allegro in 2 time, adds G/B minor); motivic - 8-12-bar unaccompanied response to a 2-bar motif; harmonic - unaccompanied over a chord sequence (4 bars x3; i, iv, V; keys D, E, F#, A, B minor). Musical knowledge (questions on own pieces): modulation to closely related keys, tonic/dominant triads, full interval names within an octave.

sections: Technical work

1) Bowing: hooked (crotchet = 88). EITHER 2) tonal centres D, F, Db/C# 3 oct (dominant 7ths 2 oct; scales separate or four beats; arpeggios separate or slurred three); chromatic from E and Db 2 oct (separate or slurred six); diminished 7ths from F and F# (separate or two beats); in thumb position 1 oct: D major, D melodic and harmonic minor scales and arpeggios. exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 5), about the end of the first year of an undergraduate course; 90 credits, 54 GLH, 900 TQT
comps: A pass at Grade 8 on the same or a closely related instrument: ABRSM Practical or Performance Grade 8, or an accepted equivalent from another board (for example Trinity, LCM, MTB, Guildhall, RIAM, AMEB or UNISA). No theory prerequisite.

Face-to-face (public venue or private visit) OR digital (video recorded at a time and place of the candidate's choice, with no fixed sessions; video uploaded at booking or within 28 days). Performance only: 30-minute programme (±2 min), timed from the first note to the last. Marks: pieces 30 (60%) + performance as a whole 20 (40%) = 50. Distinction 45–50, Merit 40–44, Pass 34–39, Below Pass 17–33.

At least 20 minutes from the ARSM repertoire list for the instrument, plus up to 10 minutes of own-choice music at Grade 8 standard or above. No written or spoken elements and no other tests (no viva, no programme notes, no quick study). Candidates submit a programme form, or enter programme details online for digital exams.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ARSM repertoire list for cello, read from the ABRSM PDF (23 entries). Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.

exams.name: ATCL
exams.full: Associate of Trinity College London (Music Performance)
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 4/5); Ofqual qualification no. 600/0949/4
comps: None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 32-38 min performing time (exam slot 40 min). Marked out of 100: Recital 96 (Fluency & accuracy 32, Technical assurance & application 32, Musical sense & communication 32) + Programme & planning 4 (written programme 2, planning/balance/construction 2). Results: Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No Merit band.

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme (composers, titles, timings) required; no full programme notes at ATCL. Trinity describes ATCL as equivalent to a first-year undergraduate recital.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ATCL repertoire list for cello, read from the Trinity PDF (48 entries). Programmes must consist of a minimum of two works, performed complete except where single movements are specified; own-choice pieces must be pre-approved. Performance durations: ATCL 32-38 min, LTCL 37-43 min, FTCL 42-48 min. Refer to the syllabus for guidance on inclusion of unaccompanied items. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction of the programme (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required at ATCL.

Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 37-43 min performing time (exam slot 45 min). Same 100-mark scheme as ATCL (96 recital + 4 programme & planning). Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79.

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required. Learning outcomes add contextual understanding and the candidate's own musical voice.

p0006.d: The famous 'Albinoni' Adagio, largely composed by Remo Giazotto in 1958 on a Baroque model: a slow, sorrowful melody over a walking bass that builds to an intense climax.
p0006.rw: Moving and familiar; little technical display

p0012.d: A short, songful lament from Arensky's set of cello pieces: a long-breathed melancholy melody in the Russian romantic tradition over a gently flowing piano part.

p0062.d: Bach's D major gamba sonata on cello, either the opening Adagio and Allegro or the closing Andante and Allegro: songful lines and lively dances with keyboard.

p0063.d: The opening Vivace of Bach's G minor gamba sonata: a concerto-like movement with driving rhythms, bold leaps and dialogue with the keyboard.

p0071.d: Three movements from Bach's G major suite: the famous Prélude with either the Allemande and Courante or the Sarabande and Gigue, giving a sunny, varied group.

p0072.d: Three movements from Bach's D minor suite: the searching Prélude with either Allemande and Courante or the intense Sarabande and driving Gigue.

p0073.d: Three movements from Bach's bright C major suite: the sweeping scale-and-arpeggio Prélude with either Allemande and Courante or Sarabande and Gigue.

p0074.d: Bach's complete E-flat suite: a sweeping, arpeggio-based Prélude followed by dances in an awkward key for cello, demanding extended hand positions and stamina.
p0074.rw: Noble suite; tricky key for intonation

p0076.d: Three dances from Bach's C major suite: a running Courante, a resonant chordal Sarabande and a lively, rustic Gigue.

p0083.d: Second and third movements of Barber's cello sonata: an Adagio with a scherzo-like Presto at its centre, then a passionate Allegro appassionato finale.
p0083.rw: Passionate and rewarding; big piano part

p0089.d: Bartók's first rhapsody (violin or cello version): a slow, swaggering lassú followed by a fast, increasingly wild friss built on folk dances.

p0090.d: Four of Bartók's Romanian Folk Dances arranged for cello: a stick dance, a sash dance, a stamping polka and a quick finale, full of folk colour.

p0095.d: Last of Beach's Three Compositions Op.40 (originally violin and piano): a lively, salon-style mazurka with a wistful middle, here played on cello.
p0095.rw: Charming, compact salon piece; less known

p0098.d: Opening Romanze of Le Beau's cello-and-piano pieces: a gentle, song-like Romantic miniature that needs a singing legato and tasteful phrasing.

p0099.d: Twelve variations on Handel's 'See, the conqu'ring hero comes', ranging from playful to brilliant; the cello and piano trade the spotlight.
p0099.rw: Witty and varied; long, piano-heavy at times

p0100.d: Seven elegant variations on the Pamina–Papageno duet from Mozart's Magic Flute; graceful Classical writing with a playful finale.
p0100.rw: Charming Mozart tune; clean Classical style shown off

p0116.d: Spacious, noble opening of the A major sonata, beginning with solo cello; lyrical breadth combined with dramatic development and wide range.
p0116.rw: Glorious, noble music; serious stamina needed

p0129.d: The compact, unusual C major sonata complete: two slow-fast pairings, mixing intimate lyricism with gruff energy; a 'free sonata' in style.

p0130.d: Vigorous, compact opening Allegro con brio of the D major sonata, full of leaping energy and abrupt dynamic contrasts.

p0131.d: Beethoven's late D major cello sonata complete: vigorous first movement, a profound Adagio and a demanding fugal finale.
p0131.rw: Profound late Beethoven; fugue very tough

p0146.d: Complete G major sonata (once attributed to Sammartini): a brisk Allegro, an expressive Grave and a lively finale, in graceful galant style.
p0146.rw: Well-loved; elegant and grateful to play

p0149.d: A set of contrasting short movements for cello and piano, written for Steven Isserlis: tuneful, witty and varied, from lyrical to energetic.

p0154.d: Bloch's solemn, deeply felt prayer for cello: a slow Jewish-inflected melody with long phrases and a heartfelt climax; tone and intensity matter most.
p0154.rw: Profoundly moving; ideal for a big tone

p0156.d: Bloch's 'Hebraic rhapsody' for cello and orchestra, voicing King Solomon: richly coloured, impassioned and declamatory, with huge emotional and technical range.

p0160.d: First movement of the B-flat concerto in Grützmacher's Romanticised version: a sweeping, extended Allegro with thumb-position brilliance and a showy cadenza.

p0166.d: The singing Adagio and brilliant Allegro of the popular A major sonata, with demanding high-register writing and nimble passagework.

p0175.d: An elegy for cello in memory of the cellist and teacher Joan Dickson: reflective and expressive, with sustained lines and gentle intensity.

p0177.d: Lili Boulanger's short, dreamy nocturne (originally violin or flute and piano), arranged for cello: hushed, sensuous Impressionist melody.

p0193.d: A single-movement set of variations for cello and orchestra (piano reduction), moving from a brooding, lyrical theme through more animated sections to a bravura close. Rich Romantic cello writing across the whole range.
p0193.rw: Rich, singing showpiece; less common than it deserves

p0204.d: The long, brooding opening movement of Brahms's first cello sonata, built on a deep, searching theme in the cello's low register. Needs sustained tone, broad phrasing and careful balance with the piano.
p0204.rw: Core repertoire; rich and deeply satisfying

p0206.d: The stormy, impassioned opening movement and the radiant, intimate Adagio of Brahms's second cello sonata. Demands big tone, rhythmic drive and long lyrical phrasing.
p0206.rw: Magnificent music; big tone and drama rewarded

p0207.d: Brahms's passionate second cello sonata: a turbulent, tremolo-driven first movement, a radiant Adagio in F sharp, a fiery scherzo and a genial rondo finale. Big, demanding and symphonic in scale.
p0207.rw: Magnificent sonata; big tone and drama rewarded

p0214.d: A tender, song-like miniature in Edwardian salon style, with a long, arching melody and warm harmonies. Tests sustained tone and expressive shaping.
p0214.rw: Lovely melody; shows off a singing tone

p0215.d: A short, light-hearted scherzo for cello and piano by Bridge, with nimble, playful figures and crisp bowing. Charming and quick rather than profound.
p0215.rw: Charming, nimble encore; short and light

p0216.d: The sweeping first movement of Bridge's cello sonata, written during the First World War: ardent, rhapsodic melodies, rich late-Romantic harmony and a densely written piano part.

p0218.d: The Moto perpetuo finale of Britten's cello sonata for Rostropovich: driving, relentless figures with jagged accents and fierce energy. Short, exciting and rhythmically exacting.
p0218.rw: Exhilarating finale; brilliant if rhythm is secure

p0223.d: The opening Canto primo and the Fuga from Britten's first solo cello suite: a chant-like, chordal refrain followed by a nimble, witty fugue on a single line.
p0223.rw: Great music; ambitious choice at this level

p0227.d: Bruch's Adagio on Hebrew melodies, built on the Kol Nidrei chant and a second theme, not a variation set. Long singing lines; needs warmth and tonal control.
p0227.rw: Much-loved; perfect for a rich, singing tone

p0237.d: A short, deeply lyrical elegy in a long-breathed, gently dissonant style. Calm and expressive, quite unlike Carter's later complex music; needs sustained tone and control.

p0240.d: A fiery Spanish-flavoured showpiece for cello and piano with relentless fast figuration and dance rhythms. Short and dazzling.

p0241.d: Cassadó's flirtatious Spanish dance for cello and piano, dedicated to Casals; seductive melodies, rhythmic swagger and brilliant passagework.

p0242.d: The first movement of Cassadó's Sonata in the old Spanish style: a stately, neo-Baroque opening with Spanish colouring and rich cello writing.

p0250.d: A cello arrangement of a melancholic Chaplin film melody: a simple, nostalgic tune needing sweet tone and expressive shaping.

p0253.d: A contemporary French piece for cello and piano exploring free, improvisatory dialogue between the instruments. Details not well known to me.

p0254.d: A meditative cello piece by Chen Yi, blending Chinese melodic inflections with Western contemporary techniques. Details not well known to me.

p0255.d: A cello piece by Chen Yi evoking Chinese instruments (the xiao flute and qin zither), with slides, folk-like melodies and gentle colour. Details not well known to me.

p0256.d: Chopin's early salon piece for cello and piano: a lyrical Introduction and a sparkling Polonaise. The piano part is the showpiece; the cello sings and flourishes in dance rhythms.

p0259.d: The broad, passionate first movement of Chopin's cello sonata: lyrical but densely written, with a demanding piano part. Requires stamina, singing tone and careful balance.
p0259.rw: Rich, passionate; balance with piano demanding

p0262.d: Chopin's late cello sonata: a dense, passionate opening Allegro, a scherzo, a short song-like Largo and a turbulent finale. Rich textures and close partnership with the piano.
p0262.rw: Major Romantic sonata; rich and passionate

p0268.d: Rebecca Clarke's passacaglia on the Tallis tune 'Song of Thomas', for cello (or viola) and piano: a solemn melody over a repeating bass, building to a powerful climax.

p0278.d: Crumb's early three-movement solo cello sonata: a Fantasia, a theme and variations and a Toccata, mixing Spanish-flavoured gestures with modernist textures.

p0279.d: The first two movements of Crumb's solo cello sonata: a dramatic, improvisatory Fantasia and a theme with variations, in a striking modern sound world.
p0279.rw: Modern classic; ambitious at this level

p0285.d: A sparkling salon showpiece depicting a playing fountain: rippling high-register spiccato and fast figuration around a sweet lyrical tune. Short but exposed.
p0285.rw: Brilliant cellist's encore; short, flashy, satisfying

p0289.d: Debussy's compact late three-movement sonata: fantastical, fleeting, with free rhythm, pizzicato colour and Spanish touches. Demands extreme colour and rhythmic flexibility.
p0289.rw: Cello masterpiece; compact, colourful, impresses examiners

p0295.d: An early, gently romantic song-like piece for cello and piano, flowing and tender with Delius's characteristic harmonic warmth. A test of legato line and tone colour.

p0297.d: A single-movement sonata of almost continuous rhapsodic melody, with a slower central section. The cello rarely rests, so stamina, line and tonal warmth matter more than virtuosity.
p0297.rw: Glorious melody, but long and unrelenting

p0307.d: A substantial single-movement concert piece for cello and orchestra (here with piano), in a lush late-Romantic Brahmsian idiom with sweeping melodies and big virtuosic passages.
p0307.rw: Rich and rewarding, but long and rarely heard

p0319.d: The concerto's slow movement: a heartfelt Adagio quoting Dvořák's song 'Leave me alone', with a stormy middle section and cadenza-like passages. Needs singing tone and emotional depth.
p0319.rw: Glorious music; shows tone and maturity

p0320.d: The outer movements of the greatest cello concerto: an heroic, symphonic opening Allegro or a march-like rondo finale with a long, nostalgic coda. Big tone and virtuosity required.
p0320.rw: Pinnacle of cello repertoire; hugely rewarding

p0322.d: The heroic first movement of the great B minor concerto: a symphonic opening, a famous lyrical second theme and passages of octaves, double stops and brilliant figuration.
p0322.rw: Pinnacle of cello repertoire; hugely rewarding

p0324.d: A lively Slavonic-flavoured rondo alternating a wistful, dance-like G minor theme with brighter episodes and quick passagework. Characterful and not too long.

p0325.d: A lively Slavonic-flavoured rondo alternating a wistful, dance-like G minor theme with brighter episodes and quick passagework. Characterful and not too long.

p0326.d: A peaceful, nocturnal song without words evoking a still Bohemian forest, with a long cantabile line and a more agitated middle section. Tests warm tone and line.
p0326.rw: Beloved cello melody; ideal lyrical choice

p0334.d: The concerto's opening: a declamatory recitative and haunting 9/8 melody, then a mercurial scherzo of rapid spiccato and repeated notes. Contrasting tone and agility.
p0334.rw: Beloved; showcases tone and bow agility

p0335.d: The concerto's brooding opening Moderato: dramatic chords, recitative and a haunting, rocking 9/8 melody. Mature and introspective rather than flashy.
p0335.rw: Iconic music; ideal for expressive players

p0336.d: Elgar's autumnal four-movement cello concerto: brooding recitatives, a quicksilver scherzo, a profound Adagio and a sweeping finale. Emotional depth plus virtuosity.

p0349.d: Piatigorsky's virtuoso arrangement of the Ritual Fire Dance: relentless driving rhythm building to a wild ending.

p0352.d: A darkly expressive C minor lament with a grave opening theme, an impassioned climax high on the instrument and a tender central section. A classic test of tone.

p0355.d: A fleet, fluttering cello encore depicting a butterfly: rapid spiccato and scale passages framing a brief lyrical middle section. Lightness and agility are key.

p0360.d: The restless, contrapuntal opening movement of Fauré's late G minor sonata, with long, searching lines over an urgent piano part. Subtle and inward rather than showy.
p0360.rw: Fine late Fauré; subtle, less immediate

p0377.d: A Baroque sonata (now attributed to Louis Francœur) in a popular cello arrangement: a noble, singing Adagio followed by a graceful Allemande-like Allegro.
p0377.rw: Classic teaching repertoire; stylish and grateful

p0379.d: A short, breathless perpetual-motion piece for cello: continuous rapid notes with Françaix's playful harmonies. A test of evenness, stamina and lightness.
p0379.rw: Fun encore; very short for a diploma

p0383.d: A grand, rhetorical cello showpiece in Baroque style; widely believed to be Cassadó's own pastiche rather than a true Frescobaldi arrangement. Bold chords and declamatory gestures.
p0383.rw: Dramatic, effective and well loved by cellists

p0390.d: Gardel's famous tango song: a sweeping, nostalgic melody over insistent tango rhythm.

p0401.d: A rhapsodic Argentine piece for cello and piano evoking the pampas: brooding, improvisatory passages and fiery dance rhythms.

p0403.d: A short, melancholy song without words for cello: a long, singing melody over a gently strummed accompaniment.
p0403.rw: Beautiful tune; rewards a singing tone

p0407.d: A brilliant, playful cello encore full of quick spiccato, leaps and high-position flourishes, with a lyrical middle section.

p0408.d: A whirlwind cello tarantella in perpetual motion, with fast bowing and crossing strings around a brief lyrical interlude.
p0408.rw: Exciting finale; demands stamina and bow control

p0409.d: A swaggering polonaise for cello: dotted dance rhythms, bold chords and nimble passagework. Romantic salon style by a cellist-composer.

p0410.d: A Romantic cello showpiece by Goltermann, mixing singing melody with lively, idiomatic passagework.
p0410.rw: Idiomatic and grateful; less well known

p0411.d: A gently Spanish-tinged song for cello: a long, wistful melody with a more animated middle section. Rewards warm tone and rubato.
p0411.rw: Lovely melody; shows a singing tone

p0441.d: Haydn's C major cello concerto first movement: buoyant, crisp Classical writing with rapid passagework and high-register runs. A cornerstone of the cello repertoire.

p0445.d: Haydn's D major concerto first movement: graceful and lyrical but notoriously exposing, with long passages in thumb position and high, delicate passagework.

p0451.d: A piece for cello and piano by English composer Anthony Hedges; as the title suggests, a dialogue between the instruments in an accessible modern idiom.

p0453.d: Henze's solo cello serenade: nine miniatures, each a sharply drawn character sketch from lyrical to playful. Five are chosen here.

p0457.d: Witty variations for cello and piano on the English nursery song, each a character sketch. Light-hearted but crisply contrapuntal and rhythmically tricky.
p0457.rw: Witty and compact; needs clean ensemble

p0465.d: Hindemith's terse solo cello sonata: five short, contrasting movements from biting and percussive to quietly lyrical. Unaccompanied and uncompromising. Two contrasting movements are chosen.

p0466.d: Hindemith's terse solo cello sonata: five short, contrasting movements from biting and percussive to quietly lyrical. Unaccompanied and uncompromising.

p0469.d: Hindemith's terse solo cello sonata: five short, contrasting movements from biting and percussive to quietly lyrical. Unaccompanied and uncompromising. Any two movements are chosen.
p0469.rw: Short but angular; exposed unaccompanied writing

p0470.d: Witty variations for cello and piano on the English nursery song, each a character sketch. Light-hearted but crisply contrapuntal and rhythmically tricky.
p0470.rw: Witty and compact; needs clean ensemble

p0471.d: A cheeky Australian piece for cello and piano with pop and disco-style grooves; rhythmic, fun and unconventional.
p0471.rw: Fun and high-energy; audiences enjoy it

p0475.d: Holst's mystical cello piece: a long, meditative melody over shimmering harmony, rising to a passionate climax.

p0476.d: A modern solo cello piece by British composer Simon Holt; likely intense and gestural, exploring the instrument's full range.

p0480.d: A brisk dance in the rigaudon style, presumably with lively dotted rhythms and crisp bowing, written by a British teacher-composer for cello and piano.

p0487.d: Opening movement of Ireland's cello sonata: brooding, richly Romantic English writing with long, surging lines and a large piano part.
p0487.rw: Deeply expressive English sonata; strong partnership needed

p0498.d: Kabalevsky's first cello concerto, written for young players: a jaunty, folk-flavoured first movement, a songful slow movement and a lively finale.

p0500.d: Kabalevsky's first cello concerto, written for young players: a jaunty, folk-flavoured first movement, a songful slow movement and a lively finale.

p0502.d: Kapustin's jazz-inspired burlesque for cello and piano: fast, syncopated and witty, written out in full classical notation but sounding improvised.
p0502.rw: Fun jazz showpiece; tight ensemble needed

p0503.d: A gentle, jazz-tinged ballad for cello and piano with rich harmonies and a long-breathed, singing line.

p0505.d: A slow, luminous song for cello and piano, building from quiet stillness to a passionate climax; originally for violin.

p0508.d: First movement of Khachaturian's cello concerto: a sweeping, rhapsodic movement full of Armenian colour, big lyrical themes and a substantial cadenza.

p0509.d: First movement of Khachaturian's cello concerto: a sweeping, rhapsodic movement full of Armenian colour, big lyrical themes and a substantial cadenza.

p0512.d: A tiny, quirky solo-cello miniature: a meandering, oddly-accented tune with a wry sense of humour.
p0512.rw: Witty miniature; short for this level

p0516.d: First movement of Kodály's monumental solo sonata: grand, declamatory and folk-tinged, with the lowest strings retuned and rich chordal writing.

p0526.d: Finale of Lalo's cello concerto: a slow introduction leading to a spirited Spanish-flavoured rondo with brilliant passagework.
p0526.rw: Spirited finale of a favourite concerto

p0527.d: Lalo's cello concerto: a dramatic, rhetorical first movement, a contrasting Intermezzo and a lively Spanish-flavoured rondo finale.

p0535.d: A late Easter-themed meditation for cello and piano by Leighton, built on plainsong: intense, mystical and richly chromatic, with ecstatic climaxes.

p0536.d: An early elegy for cello and piano: a grave, deeply felt slow piece with long singing lines.

p0546.d: Ligeti's early two-movement solo sonata: a lyrical 'Dialogo' of pizzicato and singing lines, then a fierce, virtuosic 'Capriccio'.
p0546.rw: Hugely popular modern solo; brilliant payoff

p0547.d: A Baroque sonata by Locatelli in a cello arrangement (likely Piatti's): elegant Italian slow movements and brilliant, high-lying fast movements.

p0548.d: Lutosławski's tribute to Debussy for cello and piano: a slow, ritual-like 'metamorphosis' built from a four-note motif, gradually gathering intensity.

p0553.d: MacMillan's first cello sonata: an intense single-span work combining violent outbursts with chant-like lament, in his visceral Scottish style.

p0556.d: Marais's famous variations on La Folia, edited by Maurice Gendron for cello: a stately theme followed by many inventive, increasingly virtuosic variations.

p0563.d: One of Martinů's last works: variations on a Slovak folk song for cello and piano, ranging from tender to rhythmically lively.

p0564.d: Brilliant variations on a theme from Rossini's Moses, written for Piatigorsky: witty, virtuosic and compact.

p0565.d: Zoë Martlew's cello piece with Middle-Eastern influences; likely rhythmically driven and colourful, using modern techniques.

p0567.d: Famous contemplative intermezzo from Massenet's opera Thaïs, in Marsick's violin transcription: long, singing line in D with harp-like piano, training sustained tone, vibrato and expressive shifting.

p0575.d: Bright, energetic sonata-form Allegro with a big, flowing cello line over a very busy piano part. Sunny and confident; needs a projecting tone and a strong partnership.
p0575.rw: Joyful, rewarding duo music; piano part is demanding

p0576.d: A lyrical D major theme followed by eight contrasting variations, from gentle to fiery, ending in a quiet coda. Elegant Classical-leaning Mendelssohn with plenty of rapid figuration.
p0576.rw: Charming and varied; shows control and agility

p0587.d: A warm, nostalgic sonata-form Allegro with broad Russian lyricism and late-Romantic harmony. More about singing tone and phrasing than display; an accessible yet substantial choice.

p0588.d: A deeply expressive Andante cantabile followed by a vigorous, folk-tinged finale with driving rhythms and rapid passagework. Shows both tone and agility.

p0589.d: A brief, melancholic elegy with Milhaud's characteristic bittersweet harmonies. A slow, sustained piece that relies on tone colour and expressive phrasing.

p0592.d: An unaccompanied etude evoking Broadway show tunes, with swung rhythms, chords and theatrical flair. Accessible and entertaining.

p0593.d: A wistful, lilting unaccompanied waltz with folk-like melody and chordal accompaniment woven into the cello line. Gentle and nostalgic.
p0593.rw: Lovely melody; good unaccompanied lyrical choice

p0599.d: The famous gypsy-style showpiece: a mournful slow introduction then accelerating fast sections with flashy runs, harmonics and a sultry middle part. Instantly recognisable.

p0640.d: Cassadó's arrangement of a Baroque air by Gottlieb Muffat: a noble, singing slow melody with stylish ornamentation over a rich accompaniment.

p0646.d: A single-movement Romantic concertino for cello by a German cellist-composer: tuneful, well-written and moderately virtuosic, with lyrical themes and passagework.

p0647.d: A tender, melancholic Romantic elegy for cello and piano: a long, singing melody with emotional climaxes. Hugely popular since its rediscovery.

p0650.d: Paganini's variations on a prayer from Rossini's Moses, played entirely on one string (the A string on cello). An operatic introduction followed by flashy variations with huge shifts and harmonics.

p0653.d: A bluesy, elegiac piece for cello and piano by British composer Paul Patterson, combining a lament-like melody with jazz harmony.

p0657.d: An avant-garde unaccompanied cello showpiece written for Siegfried Palm: clusters, glissandi, extreme registers and unconventional sounds. Extremely demanding.

p0658.d: A solo cello piece written for Rostropovich: brooding, intense music with dramatic outbursts and rapid figuration in a more neo-Romantic idiom.

p0661.d: Piazzolla's large, single-movement tango for cello and piano written for Rostropovich: aggressive rhythms, sensuous lyrical sections and fierce ensemble demands.

p0665.d: Popper's dazzling showpiece: a perpetual-motion of rapid, light spiccato and left-hand acrobatics across the whole range. Ultimate cello encore.

p0666.d: Popper's two best-known showpieces: Elfentanz, a whirlwind of light spiccato and rapid passagework, and Spinning Song, a buzzing perpetual motion.

p0667.d: Popper's famous rhapsody on Hungarian themes: a soulful, improvisatory slow part followed by a fast, fiery friss full of virtuoso passagework.

p0668.d: A charming Romantic salon mazurka for cello: lilting dance rhythms, elegant melody and some agile passages.

p0669.d: A graceful Romantic minuet from Popper's Op. 65 set: elegant and lightly decorated, with some delicate high work.

p0670.d: A dreamy Romantic nocturne with a long, singing melody and expressive climaxes. Tests tone and phrasing more than speed.

p0671.d: A brilliant, ceremonial polonaise: grand, dotted rhythms, virtuoso runs and lyrical interludes. Classic Romantic cello showpiece.

p0672.d: A buzzing perpetual-motion piece imitating a spinning wheel: constant fast notes and clean left-hand work.

p0675.d: Poulenc's much-loved flute sonata (1957): a wistful, songful first movement, a haunting Cantilena and a sparkling, cheeky Presto finale.
p0675.rw: Much-loved French sonata; strong recital centrepiece

p0685.d: Arrangement of the menacing 'Dance of the Knights' from Prokofiev's Romeo and Juliet. Heavy dotted rhythms and a grand, dramatic sweep; very recognisable.
p0685.rw: Famous tune; dramatic and fun to play

p0689.d: First movement of Prokofiev's Cello Sonata: a broad, singing opening melody that grows into vigorous, rhythmic music. Warm and lyrical, exploiting the cello's full range.

p0693.d: Second and third movements of Prokofiev's Cello Sonata: a witty, dance-like Moderato with a lyrical centre, then a festive, bold finale with high-lying passagework.

p0694.d: Prokofiev's Cello Sonata complete: warm lyricism, a playful middle movement and a festive finale. Generous, appealing music across the cello's whole range.

p0696.d: Pärt's meditative tintinnabuli piece (1977), arranged for many instruments: a chant-like sequence of variations separated by drone-like pauses. Hypnotic and atmospheric.
p0696.rw: Atmospheric and striking; a memorable recital item

p0704.d: First two movements of Rachmaninov's Cello Sonata: a passionate, expansive opening Allegro and a restless, driving scherzo with a lyrical trio. The piano part is enormous.
p0704.rw: Romantic cello essential; huge emotional payoff

p0706.d: Finale of Rachmaninov's Cello Sonata: an energetic, festive Allegro mosso with a broad, soaring second theme. Demanding passagework and stamina against a heavy piano part.
p0706.rw: Exciting finale; requires a strong pianist

p0709.d: Arrangement of Ravel's Pavane: a slow, stately, melancholy melody over gentle harmonies. Demands a beautifully controlled singing line rather than technical display.

p0718.d: Präludium from Reger's second solo cello suite: Bach-inspired, with flowing figuration and chordal writing in a richer late-Romantic harmonic language.
p0718.rw: Solid unaccompanied choice; Bach-like but Romantic

p0742.d: Saint-Saëns's Allegro appassionato, originally for cello: a spirited, restless showpiece with racing passagework and a warm, lyrical second theme. Short and effective.

p0745.d: Opening section of Saint-Saëns's First Cello Concerto: a dramatic, driving start with flowing triplet figuration and a lyrical second theme. Compact and effective.

p0747.d: First two sections of Saint-Saëns's single-span First Cello Concerto: the dramatic, driving opening and the graceful, minuet-like Allegretto.

p0771.d: Schubert's Arpeggione Sonata: a melancholy opening, a song-like Adagio and a genial finale. High-lying writing and wide arpeggios challenge the player.

p0777.d: Five contrasting pieces 'in folk style', ranging from rustic humour to tender song and a vigorous finale. Charming rather than virtuosic, so the challenge is character and colour.
p0777.rw: Charming but modest showcase for diploma level

p0779.d: A slow, warmly lyrical Adagio followed by an exuberant, surging Allegro. Originally for horn, it needs stamina, big tone and sweeping Romantic phrasing.
p0779.rw: Popular recital piece; big Romantic payoff

p0780.d: Opening movement of Schumann's intensely lyrical concerto: restless, passionate and continuous, with long melodies and demanding passagework in high positions.
p0780.rw: Core cello concerto; rewards mature musicianship

p0781.d: Schumann's cello concerto played as one continuous span: passionate first movement, short intimate slow movement and a tricky, energetic finale with accompanied cadenza.
p0781.rw: Core repertoire; finale is awkward but rewarding

p0784.d: Three short, linked character pieces moving from dreamy and tender to warm, then to a fiery, driving finale. Originally for clarinet; needs rich tone and sustained Romantic phrasing.
p0784.rw: Beloved Romantic set; showcases tone and musicianship

p0789.d: A sombre, meditative lament for solo cello, drawing on Sculthorpe's Australian landscape-inspired sound world with slow, keening lines.

p0792.d: Unaccompanied cello pieces based on Chinese folk songs, using pizzicato, glissandi and drone effects; 'Guessing Song' is playful, 'Tibetan Dance' fast and rhythmically driving.

p0796.d: Complete concerto: biting opening Allegretto, haunting slow movement, a long solo cadenza and a frantic finale. One of the great modern cello concertos.

p0798.d: Outer movements of Shostakovich's cello sonata: a broad, lyrical first movement with a stark, eerie close, and a deeply melancholy Largo.
p0798.rw: Masterpiece of the repertoire; deeply rewarding

p0799.d: Opening movement of the cello sonata: broadly lyrical with a darker, more restless development and a strange, slow-motion coda.

p0800.d: A lilting, nostalgic waltz from Shostakovich's light ballet music, arranged for cello and piano. Graceful and tuneful, with room for expressive shaping.

p0803.d: A theme and variations for cello and piano by Sibelius; an early, lyrical work, little known and modest in display.
p0803.rw: Rare early piece; little performance tradition

p0805.d: Short, slow pieces in Skempton's spare, quietly radiant style: simple lines and harmonies where pure tone and stillness matter more than display.

p0810.d: An intense, lamenting piece for solo cello where the player also sings or hums, blending Sicilian folk lament with modern effects; slow keening gives way to driving rhythms.
p0810.rw: Haunting and striking; very popular now

p0813.d: A salon piece for cello and piano by cellist W. H. Squire: graceful ballroom character with idiomatic, showy writing that lies well on the instrument.

p0817.d: The lively, good-humoured finale of the young Strauss's cello sonata: energetic rondo-style writing with a fugal section and plenty of Romantic sweep.

p0825.d: A slow, prayer-like lament on Jewish themes by cellist-composer Joachim Stutschewsky; deeply expressive with cantorial-style ornament.

p0827.d: An early, dramatic ballade for cello and piano, Dvořák-influenced, alternating stormy and lyrical sections.

p0829.d: A gentle, lyrical serenade for cello and piano from Suk's student years, warm and songful in Dvořák's style.

p0838.d: Kochański's transcription of Roxana's sensuous aria from King Roger, played on cello: languid, ornamented melody that climbs high over rich, exotic harmonies.

p0857.d: A short virtuoso piece in B minor: a brooding, lyrical theme followed by flashy spiccato and high-lying passagework. Compact but technically treacherous.

p0860.d: Elegant theme with seven variations in a Mozartian spirit but full of Romantic display: lyrical slow variations, sparkling fast ones and high-lying virtuoso writing.

p0872.d: An energetic, driving piece by Joan Tower for cello, built on restless rhythmic momentum and bold gestures across the range.
p0872.rw: Exciting modern showcase for rhythmic players

p0882.d: A hushed, haunting movement for solo cello in which the player also sings in falsetto above the instrument, creating an ethereal, prayer-like atmosphere.
p0882.rw: Mesmerising and unusual; memorable in recital

p0898.d: A whirling, energetic piece by Errollyn Wallen inspired by the spinning of Sufi dervishes, with driving rhythms and hypnotic repetition.

p0900.d: Walton's cello concerto: a dreamy, bittersweet opening Moderato, then either a fiery, virtuosic Scherzo or a set of improvisatory variations on a lyrical theme.

p0901.d: First movement of Walton's concerto: dreamy, bittersweet lyricism over a restless accompaniment, with glittering, demanding passagework and wide expressive range.

p0906.d: A short, tender night-piece for cello and piano with a warm, songful melody and gently lush English harmonies.
p0906.rw: Beautiful lyrical piece; tonal control showcase

p0907.d: An early, intense cello sonata by Weill, before his theatre years: dense, chromatic and restless, with angular lines and a driving energy.

p0908.d: A suite of short pieces for solo cello based on American folk songs recorded from prisoners; spare, poignant and rhythmically characterful.

p0933.d: A lyrical cello piece by Wilson; the title suggests a warm, romantic character, likely song-like with intertwining lines.

p0675|Cello.d: Poulenc's Cello Sonata (1940–48), a larger four-movement work: a march-like opening, a tender Cavatine, a playful Ballabile and a dramatic finale.
p0675|Cello.rw: Warm, witty and less often heard than the flute sonata

p0901|Cello.d: First movement (Moderato) of Walton's Cello Concerto (1956): a slow, glowing lyrical movement that asks for a long singing line high on the instrument.

s0001.d: Beach's tender lullaby in a cello version: a rocking accompaniment under a long, arching melody. Demands tonal control and expressive shaping more than technical display.

s0008.d: A short, song-like piece from a set of four love songs for cello. Gentle and lyrical, focusing on smooth legato and tone.

s0010.d: An arranged sentimental salon-style piece evoking evening bells. Slow and expressive, practising sustained tone and smooth shifting.

s0016.d: A lively second movement from one of Alessandro Scarlatti's cello sonatas. Clear Baroque figuration, needing even passagework and crisp articulation.

s0021.d: An unaccompanied American-style cello etude imitating a train whistle, using slides and folk/blues-inflected figures. Rhythmic and fun.

s0022.d: An unaccompanied pop-influenced cello piece from Minsky's Pop Goes the Cello. Upbeat, rock-style rhythms and drive.

s0025.d: A slow, song-like movement from a Basque-flavoured Serenade. Lyrical and expressive, focusing on tone and phrasing.

s0026.d: A Spanish-flavoured dance with strong rhythms and colourful character. Practises rhythmic drive and articulation.

s0027.d: A tango-inspired piece by the Argentine composer Adriana Figueroa Mañas. Sultry, rhythmic and expressive, with typical tango accents and rubato.

s0033.d: A busy, energetic moto-perpetuo-style piece from McDonagh's It's a Cello Thing. Practises fast fingers and clean string crossings.

s0035.d: A cheerful, bouncy dance with an Italian flavour from It's a Cello Thing, Book 1. Practises lively rhythm and clear bowing.
s0035.rw: Cheerful and popular with young cellists

s0036.d: A flowing, atmospheric piece from It's a Cello Thing, Book 1. Practises smooth legato and gentle shifts.

s0037.d: A bright, march-like piece from It's a Cello Thing, Book 1. Practises steady rhythm and confident bowing.

s0038.d: An expressive, travelling piece from It's a Cello Thing, Book 2. Lyrical lines with some shifting.

s0039.d: A gentle, wistful Initial-grade piece from Bullard's Party Time! (slurs optional). Practises sustained tone.

s0040.d: A short Hungarian-flavoured dance from Party Time!. Lively rhythm and contrast; good for clear, accented bowing.

s0041.d: A jolly hoedown-style piece from Party Time!. Practises steady rhythm and open strings.

s0043.d: Arrangement of the Beauty and the Beast title song for cello. Lyrical and familiar; practises smooth bowing and tone.

s0047.d: Slow and fast movements from a cello sonata by the Baroque virtuoso Alborea (Francischello). Expressive Adagio then a lively Vivace.

s0048.d: A light, playful Classical-style movement by Albrechtsberger. Practises neat articulation and clear rhythm.

s0050.d: Two movements from an easy Baroque cello sonata by Aldrovandini. A slow Largo then a lively Allegro.

s0053.d: A stately, Renaissance-style pavane for Initial grade, used across all four string instruments. Practises slow, even bowing.

s0059.d: Andrée's Romance, arranged for cello. Gentle and lyrical.

s0063.d: An arranged hornpipe. Lively dance rhythms and crisp bowing.

s0064.d: Arrangement of an Italian rant (a lively folk dance). Brisk rhythm and simple bowing.

s0065.d: A simple arrangement of La Bergamasca, a famous Renaissance dance tune. Practises steady rhythm and bowing.

s0066.d: Arrangement of an American folk song (Hi! Says the Blackbird). Gentle, cheerful melody.

s0067.d: A Czech folk song duet from a cello method book. Simple, singing melody.

s0069.d: Arrangement of the canon Dona Nobis Pacem. Calm and flowing; practises legato.

s0071.d: An arranged hornpipe from Violoncello Music for Beginners. Lively and rhythmic.

s0072.d: A simple song arrangement from Stringsongs for Cello. Practises open strings and rhythm.

s0073.d: A Hungarian dance from a historical tablature manuscript. Rhythmic and folk-flavoured.

s0074.d: A Hungarian leaping dance from a historical manuscript. Lively and rhythmic.

s0075.d: A simple arrangement of the round Frère Jacques. Practises steady rhythm.

s0078.d: A Provençal dance played as a cello duet. Lively and rhythmic.

s0082.d: Arrangement of Branle des Sabots from Arbeau's Orchésographie (1589). A simple Renaissance dance.

s0089.d: A grumpy, characterful Arens piece (duet or piano). Fun for younger players.

s0090.d: A jazzy Arens piece over an ostinato. Practises swing rhythm.

s0095.d: Arensky's Petite ballade for cello. A melancholy melody with a lyrical shape.

s0097.d: Two contrasting movements from Ariosti's viola d'amore Lessons, edited for cello by Piatti: a broad, ornamented Adagio and a flowing Allemanda in E minor. Rewards poise and a clean, singing line.
s0097.rw: Elegant Baroque pair; less familiar than Marcello or Vivaldi

s0104.d: Arrangement of Harold Arlen's march-like song from The Wizard of Oz (1939); a cheerful, bouncy tune that practises steady rhythm and clean string crossings. Abracadabra cello version, playable as a duet or with piano.
s0104.rw: Familiar tune; duet option is appealing

s0106.d: Thomas Arne's graceful 18th-century Air arranged for cello. A gentle, song-like piece in English Baroque/early Classical style, focused on smooth legato and tasteful phrasing.
s0106.rw: Pleasant lyrical choice; modest technical payoff

s0107.d: Arutiunian's Armenian-flavoured Impromptu for cello: a rhapsodic, melodic piece with folk-like inflections and a more energetic central section. Needs a rich tone and confident shifting.
s0107.rw: Colourful, characterful; shows off tone and temperament

s0114.d: Henry VIII's Tudor song 'Pastime with good company', arranged for cello with a second verse. A robust, dance-like melody with a folk/early-music flavour.

s0120.d: Cello version of the popular 'Paradis' Sicilienne (probably by Samuel Dushkin). A gentle, lilting melody with a touch of melancholy; tests sustained tone, vibrato and some tenor clef reading.
s0120.rw: Much loved; shows off a singing tone

s0121.d: Pair of lively tambourins by the French Baroque composer Jacques Aubert, arranged for cello. Bright, drum-like dances with a contrasting second section; practises crisp rhythm and bow control.

s0122.d: Tor Aulin's Elegy arranged for cello: a melancholy, song-like late Romantic piece from his set of short character pieces. Rewards a rich tone and expressive rubato.
s0122.rw: Attractive Romantic miniature; less well known

s0123.d: A complete short Baroque sonata from a collection of 'easy sonatas', played from the upper part. Several brief contrasting movements build style and stamina rather than virtuosity.

s0124.d: Lively second movement of Benedetto Marcello's E minor cello sonata. Energetic Baroque writing with sequences and crisp articulation; a mainstay of early cello repertoire.

s0129.d: First two movements of Marcello's G major cello sonata: a lyrical, ornamented Adagio and a lively, buoyant Allegro. Straightforward Baroque style good for tone and articulation.

s0134.d: Lively finale of Marcello's C major cello sonata: bright, dance-like Baroque writing with running passages and some string crossing.

s0141.d: Arrangement for cello of the well-known March in D from the Anna Magdalena Bach Notebook (attributed to C. P. E. Bach). Bright and confident, practising rhythm and clear articulation.

s0146.d: Bach's famous 'Air on the G String' (from Orchestral Suite No. 3) for cello. A slow, serene melody with long phrases that tests sustained bowing and tone.

s0167.d: Simple arrangement of a chorale from Bach's St Matthew Passion. Slow and hymn-like, practising smooth, sustained tone and even phrasing.

s0172.d: Simple cello arrangement of an aria from Bach's Peasant Cantata. A short, friendly tune practising steady rhythm and tone.

s0173.d: A simple Bach-based piece from an Essential String Method book, arranged by Nelson for beginners. Likely a call-and-response style melody practising basic bowing and pulse.

s0178.d: Suzuki cello arrangement of the Arioso (Sinfonia) from Bach's Cantata 156. Slow, tender and long-breathed, demanding sustained tone and gentle shaping.

s0179.d: Suzuki cello arrangement of the Gavotte in C minor from Bach's fifth cello suite. A dignified dance practising rhythm and clear articulation.

s0181.d: Suzuki cello arrangement of the Musette from Bach's English Suite No. 3, with its drone-like bass imitating bagpipes. Bright, rustic and dance-like.

s0972.d: A graceful gavotte arranged for two cellos, played as a duet; teaches ensemble listening, steady pulse and neat upbeat phrasing.
s0972.rw: Pleasant duet; good for ensemble skills

s0973.d: Simplified arrangement of the famous Hallelujah Chorus from Messiah; bold, rhythmic and instantly recognisable, needing confident, ringing bow strokes.

s0978.d: Arrangement of Polyphemus's comic bass aria from Acis and Galatea; bustling and jaunty, with lively running quavers and character.
s0978.rw: Characterful aria; great fit for cello

s0982.d: A slow, stately sarabande arranged as a cello duet; broad triple-time phrases with emphasis on the second beat, building tone and ensemble.
s0982.rw: Noble melody; good for tone work

s0983.d: Opening Adagio from a sonata in C attributed to Handel, arranged for cello; a slow, expressive movement focusing on sustained tone and ornamented line.

s0984.d: Final Allegro of the same Handel sonata in C; lively Baroque passagework with sequences and string crossings, needing clean articulation.

s0986.d: Simple arrangement of 'See, the conquering hero comes' from Judas Maccabaeus; a proud, march-like tune with clear phrasing.

s0990.d: Simple Stringsongs arrangement of a Handel gavotte with duet or piano; light upbeat dance in early positions.

s0993.d: The Suzuki Bourrée: a lively Baroque dance in duple time with a buoyant, detached character; practises crisp articulation and light, even phrasing.

s0997.d: An easy arrangement of a well-known Water Music theme; bright and festive, building steady rhythm and simple bowing.

s1002.d: Arrangement of the swashbuckling Pirates of the Caribbean theme; driving rhythm in compound time with strong accents and energy.
s1002.rw: Huge student favourite; energetic and fun

s1003.d: Arrangement of Charles K. Harris's 1892 waltz song; a nostalgic, sentimental tune in lilting triple time with gentle swells.
s1003.rw: Charming period waltz; good for phrasing

s1004.d: Two very short tutor-book pieces from Cello Basics (a choice of one); simple tunes building basic bowing and early finger patterns.

s1007.d: Choice of two short tutor pieces from Cello Basics: a chugging train piece or a lively hornpipe; both build rhythmic bowing.

s1009.d: Arrangement of a Hasse bourrée; a cheerful Baroque duple-time dance practising clean detached strokes.

s1022.d: An easy Haydn Allegro arranged as a cello duet; bright, Classical-style phrases teaching ensemble and clear articulation.

s1026.d: A brisk Haydn scherzo-finale arranged for two cellos; playful, rhythmic and well suited to ensemble work.

s1028.d: A short Haydn minuet in D for cello with da capo; poised Classical dance practising balanced phrasing and clean bowing.

s1030.d: A Haydn minuet and trio arranged by Sheila Nelson, played without da capo; poised Classical phrasing in triple time.

s1031.d: Arrangement of the slow movement of Haydn's 'Emperor' Quartet, whose theme became the German national anthem; slow and noble, needing smooth legato and even tone.

s1034.d: First movement of a Haydn baryton trio arranged for cello and piano; a playful, elegant Classical movement.

s1035.d: Easy arrangement of the famous Andante from Haydn's Surprise Symphony; a simple tune with a playful sudden loud chord.

s1046.d: A short, gentle lullaby-like piece (by the title) arranged for cello; calm melody focusing on smooth bowing.

s1048.d: Arrangement of 'Tom Bowling' (Dibdin's song) as used in Henry Wood's Fantasia on British Sea Songs; a slow, mournful lament.

s1053.d: Arrangement of Nigel Hess's yearning main theme from the 2004 film Ladies in Lavender; a sustained, nostalgic melody that needs a warm, singing tone and secure control of the upper register.

s1055.d: A Latin-style Rumba by Tony Hewitt-Jones; syncopated rhythms in a cheerful dance mood.

s1057.d: Final lively piece from Hindemith's Three Easy Pieces for cello and piano (1938); crisp, energetic writing with Hindemith's spiky tonal language.

s1065.d: Simple arrangement of Augusta Holmès's Christmas song Noël ('Trois anges sont venus ce soir'); a gentle, lilting carol melody.

s1067.d: Arrangement of the stately 'Thaxted' hymn tune from Jupiter in The Planets. A broad, noble melody that needs a full, sustained tone and long phrasing.
s1067.rw: Famous tune; builds a big singing cello sound

s1069.d: Simple cello arrangement of the big hymn tune from Holst's Jupiter. Slow and singing, good for practising smooth bow changes and sustained tone.

s1074.d: Easy cello arrangement of a graceful minuet-style movement by James Hook; elegant triple-time phrasing and clean articulation.

s1075.d: A tender Irish-flavoured slow air for cello and piano; expressive and singing, rewarding a warm tone and shaped phrasing.
s1075.rw: Heartfelt melody; shows off cello tone

s1076.d: Stephen Hough's lively companion to Angelic Song: a bright, rhythmic dance needing agile bowing and confident shifting.
