s1775.d: Rameau's famous Tambourin, imitating pipe and drum with a drone-like bass and a quick, perky tune. Practises fast, light articulation and steady rhythm.
s1775.rw: Catchy, famous tune; lively and fun

s1783.d: A short, wistful Russian melody by Rebikov, arranged for cello. Practises a sustained, singing tone and gentle phrasing in a minor key.
s1783.rw: Touching small melody; good for tone

s1790.d: Quick finale of a Reinagle sonatina for cello, cheerful and Classical in style. Practises clean string crossings, steady rhythm and lively détaché.

s1810.d: A simple arrangement of the tender Rodgers & Hammerstein waltz from The Sound of Music. Practises smooth legato and gentle triple time.
s1810.rw: Much-loved tune; easy to play musically

s1811.d: Rodgers and Hammerstein's title song from The Sound of Music (1959), a wide-ranging flowing tune opening with rising leaps. Practises warm tone and long phrases.

s1823.d: First movement of Romberg's popular E minor cello sonata: a melancholy, flowing Allegro with scales, arpeggios and some higher positions. A staple of intermediate cello teaching.

s1829.d: A short mazurka for cello and piano from a set of Miniatures, with accented triple-time Polish dance rhythms. Practises rhythmic character and phrasing.

s1830.d: A lively Transylvanian folk-style dance from Ros Stephen's Cello Globetrotters, inspired by Romanian/Hungarian stick dances. Practises driving rhythm and crisp bowing.

s1834.d: A playful jive-style beginner cello piece from a New Zealand collection, with a cheeky title nodding to a Kiwi joke. Practises steady rhythm and lively bowing.

s1839.d: Rossini's 'A Tear' (Une larme) in a cello version: a lament-like theme with variations of growing brilliance. Needs a singing tone and expressive operatic phrasing.
s1839.rw: Operatic, expressive; rewards a big tone

s1840.d: Arrangement of Nino Rota's love theme from The Godfather. A brooding, melancholy minor-key melody practising expressive legato.

s1841.d: A relaxed swing piece from Roy McCormack's Let's Swing for cello. Practises swung rhythm and a laid-back feel.

s1843.d: Arrangement of Rubinstein's famous 'Melody in F', a broad, singing salon tune over a flowing accompaniment. Needs a warm, sustained cantabile and smooth shifts.
s1843.rw: Instantly likeable tune; showcases cantabile tone

s1847.d: Unaccompanied cello piece by a British composer, presumably evoking the Dartmoor tor of its title. Calls for confident tone colour and pacing alone on stage.

s1851.d: Short, playful beginner piece with a nonsense-rhyme title from Sheila Nelson's Piece by Piece. Builds secure open-string and simple finger patterns.

s1863.d: A cheerful, happy tune from Piece by Piece, suitable for violin or cello beginners. Practises smooth bowing and simple finger patterns.

s1864.d: A swing-style tune from Tetratunes on simple notes, played with duet or piano. Introduces swung rhythm and a relaxed groove.
s1864.rw: Fun jazzy groove; popular with beginners

s1865.d: Lively Technitunes piece with a jazzy, bouncy feel, played without the improvisation section. Practises rhythm and bow agility.

s1867.d: First movement of Paxton's A major cello sonata, an elegant galant Allegro with running passagework and higher positions. Needs stylish, clean playing.
s1867.rw: Stylish classical sonata; less familiar choice

s1868.d: Opening movement of a light classical cello sonata, with graceful melodies and running passages. Develops neat articulation and style.

s1869.d: Cheerful galant movement from Paxton's 'easy solos', with tuneful phrases and simple passagework. Ideal introduction to classical style.
s1869.rw: Attractive and idiomatic; well suited to Grade 3

s1874.d: Saenger's pastoral miniature with a Scottish flavour, in Willeke's cello arrangement. A gentle, lilting salon piece needing a lovely tone.
s1874.rw: Charming salon piece, free score available

s1875.d: Saint-Saëns's famous 'Swan', a serene, long-breathed melody over rippling piano. Simple on paper but exposes tone, bow control and intonation.

s1876.d: Saint-Saëns's famous 'Swan', a serene, long-breathed melody over rippling piano. Simple on paper but exposes tone, bow control and intonation.

s1877.d: Choice of two Saint-Saëns slow pieces: the devout, hymn-like Prière or the elegant, songlike Romance. Both reward a warm cantabile and phrasing.

s1878.d: An elegant, songful Romance originally for horn, flowing gracefully with a touch of melancholy. Needs a singing tone and smooth, connected phrasing.
s1878.rw: Elegant melody; good showcase for tone

s1880.d: Simplified arrangement of the elephant's lumbering waltz from Carnival of the Animals. Practises steady 3/4 and full, heavy tone.

s1881.d: Arrangement of Saint-Saëns's spooky Danse macabre, a ghostly waltz. Practises rhythmic drive and character.

s1892.d: Arrangement of Satie's cabaret-style song 'At the Doctor's', with witty, music-hall charm. Practises rhythm and character.

s1898.d: A graceful classical cello duet movement by Schetky, played as a duet. Practises ensemble and stylish articulation.

s1901.d: A simple, songlike piece from Schlemüller's Six Easy Concert Pieces, warm and lyrical. Practises sustained tone and smooth bowing.

s1913.d: Arrangement of Schubert's famous Serenade, a wistful, longing melody. Needs lyrical tone and expressive phrasing.

s1916.d: Arrangement of Schubert's sprightly song The Trout. Practises light articulation and clear rhythm.

s1918.d: Cello arrangement of Schubert's An die Musik, a heartfelt, warm melody. Practises legato and tone.

s1921.d: A contemporary French cello piece from Billaudot's Panorama series, probably exploring modern techniques. Needs rhythmic precision and colour.

s1930.d: Suzuki arrangement of Schumann's song Die beiden Grenadiere, dramatic and march-like. Practises dotted rhythms and character.

s1934.d: A simple Schumann melody arranged as a cello duet, light and cheerful. Practises smooth bowing and ensemble.

s0204.d: A cello duet arrangement of the cheerful, bouncing song 'Consider Yourself' from Lionel Bart's musical Oliver!. Rhythmic ensemble playing is the focus.
s0204.rw: Familiar show tune; fun ensemble piece

s0205.d: An easy arrangement of the heartfelt ballad 'As Long as He Needs Me' from Oliver!. Practises a sustained singing line.

s0209.d: A cello arrangement of the first piece from Bartók's 'For Children', a simple Hungarian folk tune. Steady and plain, ideal for early tone and intonation.
s0209.rw: Authentic folk tune; simple and honest

s0210.d: Two of Bartók's Romanian Folk Dances for cello: the vigorous stick dance and the haunting 'Buciumeana' with its exotic, high-register melody. Strong folk character.
s0210.rw: Famous, characterful pieces; audiences love them

s0215.d: Two contrasting Romanian Folk Dances: the bright, stamping Sash Dance and the static, eerie 'In One Spot' with its exotic melody. Colourful and very recognisable.

s0217.d: Two short folk-tune arrangements from 'For Children': a lilting girls' song and a comic, swaggering drinking song. Good for contrast of mood.

s0218.d: A cello arrangement of a simple folk tune from Bartók's 'For Children', Vol. 2. Gentle, songful and modal.

s0221.d: Easy cello duet arrangements of short Bartók folk-based pieces. Choose a Hungarian song or a cheeky teasing song; good for ensemble playing.
s0221.rw: Real Bartók folk flavour; simple duet

s0222.d: A simple, calm cello duet arranged from a Bartók folk-style piece, evoking a summer night. Practises steady, quiet bowing.
s0222.rw: Gentle duet; easy introduction to Bartók

s0225.d: The 19th-century song 'Long, Long Ago' by T. H. Bayly from Suzuki Book 1. A gentle tune with a simple variation, practising tone and string crossings.
s0225.rw: Familiar Suzuki staple; solid tone builder

s0227.d: A lively French folk-dance movement from Bazelaire's 'Suite française'. Rustic, stamping rhythms and energetic bowing.
s0227.rw: Spirited and rustic; good for energy

s0238.d: A dreamy, romantic character piece from Hugo Becker's suite 'Liebesleben' for cello. Expressive lyricism and singing tone.
s0238.rw: Lovely salon piece by a cello master

s0244.d: A cheerful folk-song setting from Beethoven's British folk song arrangements, arranged for cello. Jaunty, toast-like character.
s0244.rw: Jolly folk song; fun and accessible

s0248.d: An arrangement of Beethoven's tender love song 'Ich liebe dich' (Zärtliche Liebe). Simple, warm melody needing smooth legato.
s0248.rw: Lovely tune; ideal for tone building

s0249.d: A cello arrangement of one of Beethoven's Irish folk song settings. Simple, songful melody.

s0256.d: A short, melancholy sonatina originally for mandolin and keyboard, arranged for cello. Gentle, poignant phrasing.

s0260.d: An arrangement of Beethoven's song 'Gretels Warnung' (Gretel's Warning) for cello. Simple, songful and gently dramatic.

s0262.d: A beginners' arrangement of Beethoven's 'Ode to Joy'. Simple step-wise tune for early string players.

s0264.d: Beethoven's famous Minuet in G in the Suzuki cello arrangement. Graceful and elegant, practising clean shifting and dance style.

s0270.d: Very simple cello duets from Benoy & Burrowes's First-Year method: a rocking 'To and Fro' or a calm 'Meditation'.

s0271.d: A bold, marching duet from Benoy & Burrowes's First-Year Violoncello Method. Strong rhythm and confident bowing.

s0279.d: An arrangement of 'Maria' from Bernstein's West Side Story. Soaring, romantic melody with a famous tritone opening.

s0280.d: An arrangement of 'America' from West Side Story, with its famous alternating 6/8 and 3/4 rhythms. Energetic and Latin-flavoured.

s0281.d: A choice of 'Cool' (tense, jazzy) or 'I Feel Pretty' (light, waltzing) from West Side Story. Both need character and rhythmic flair.

s0283.d: An arrangement of the yearning ballad 'Somewhere' from West Side Story. Broad, lyrical melody needing sustained tone.

s0290.d: A gentle, lyrical original piece for cello from the Grade by Grade series, evoking a flowering wisteria. Smooth legato.

s1945.d: Newly written lyrical piece for the ABRSM 2024 cello syllabus, evoking the flowering hibiscus of Chengdu, likely with a pentatonic, Chinese-inflected melody. Focuses on singing tone and expressive phrasing.
s1945.rw: Fresh, atmospheric melody; good for tone

s1950.d: Arrangement of the Romance from Shostakovich's 1955 film score The Gadfly: a long, yearning, song-like melody over gentle accompaniment, training sustained tone and expressive phrasing.
s1950.rw: Hugely popular tune; great for tone

s1955.d: Gentle, songful Romance from Sibelius's Op. 78 pieces, with a long Nordic melody and a passionate central climb. Calls for a sustained singing line, shifting and expressive rubato.
s1955.rw: Fine Sibelius miniature; rewards lyrical playing

s1956.d: Sibelius's Romance Op. 78 No. 2 for cello: a tender, flowing melody rising to a warm climax. A strong test of legato, shifting and expressive vibrato.

s1960.d: Arrangement of Harold Fraser-Simson's setting of A. A. Milne's poem 'Halfway Down' (from When We Were Very Young). A gentle, simple song tune ideal for first-stage cellists.

s1963.d: Cello transcription of Scriabin's piano Prelude Op. 35 No. 2: a lilting, slightly melancholic piece with restless harmonies. Needs flexible phrasing and subtle tone colour.

s1968.d: Simplified cello arrangement of the main theme of Smetana's 'Vltava' (The Moldau): the broad, flowing river melody in E minor. Practises legato, smooth string crossings and long phrases.
s1968.rw: Famous melody; very appealing for students

s1971.d: Choice of two pieces from Springthorpe's Go with the Flow: a busy, bustling city-street piece or a Spanish-tinged homage evoking Rodrigo's Aranjuez. Contemporary light-music style.
s1971.rw: Accessible light-music style; easy to enjoy

s1972.d: A charming salon miniature by the cellist-composer W. H. Squire: a light, song-like melody with gentle Edwardian charm. Practises lyrical phrasing and graceful bowing.
s1972.rw: Idiomatic cello salon piece; teacher favourite

s1973.d: Squire's bright, cheeky Danse rustique: a bouncing rustic dance with off-string bowing, quick shifts and humour. A popular student showpiece.
s1973.rw: Perennial favourite; shows off bow agility

s1974.d: A witty gavotte by Squire with playful rhythms, staccato and humorous surprises. A test of crisp articulation, bow control and character.

s1975.d: A gently rocking Venetian boat song by Squire in 6/8: a lilting, singing melody with expressive shifts. Practises legato and warm vibrato.

s1976.d: Squire's lively Humoresque: playful and quick, with jaunty rhythms, spiccato and a contrasting lyrical section. Shows bow agility and character.

s1977.d: A spirited Polish-style mazurka by Squire with dotted rhythms and accented beats, contrasted with lyrical passages. Practises rhythmic character and agile shifting.
s1977.rw: Characterful dance; well suited to cello

s1978.d: A graceful, old-fashioned minuet by Squire: poised triple time, neat articulation and elegant phrasing. Good for bow control and style.

s1979.d: A short, songful Romance by Squire: a simple, expressive cello melody with gentle piano support. Develops tone, legato and early vibrato.
s1979.rw: Lovely singing piece for developing cellists

s1980.d: Squire's Romance Op. 5 No. 1: a tender, flowing melody well suited to the cello's middle register. Practises long phrases, legato shifts and warm tone.
s1980.rw: Idiomatic lyrical piece; rewards good tone

s1981.d: Squire's Sérénade Op. 15: an elegant, charming salon serenade with a lilting melody, some pizzicato-style accompaniment feel and expressive high-register writing.

s1982.d: Squire's fizzing Tarantella Op. 23: a rapid 6/8 dance full of running notes, spiccato and bravura passages. A classic student showpiece for the cello.

s1987.d: A graceful, light-footed Allegretto by John Stanley arranged for cello: a charming Georgian-era tune in a moderate tempo. Practises neat articulation and elegant phrasing.
s1987.rw: Pleasant Baroque piece; good for style

s1988.d: A simple tune from Stanley Fletcher's New Tunes for Strings, played with a repeat using a set bowing variation. Builds basic open-string and first-finger patterns with rhythm.
s1988.rw: Standard beginner choice; useful bowing practice

s1995.d: Arrangement of the tender aria 'Bist du bei mir' (by Stölzel, from Anna Magdalena Bach's notebook): a calm, devotional melody in long phrases. Demands sustained tone and simple elegance.

s1997.d: Cello arrangement of Johann Strauss I's famous Radetzky March: a jaunty, martial tune with dotted rhythms and clear accents. Practises crisp rhythm and strong bow strokes.
s1997.rw: Very familiar; fun but limited depth

s2006.d: Rezső Sugár's simple arrangement of an old Hungarian folk song for beginner cello: a plaintive modal melody in first position. Practises tone and simple phrasing.

s2007.d: Beginner cello setting of an old Hungarian folk song by Sugár, from the EMB beginners' book: short modal tune in first position building tone and steady bowing.

s2011.d: Marco's tenor song from Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers (English), a graceful, lilting number in light Italianate style; practises legato, light tone and diction.
s2011.rw: Charming tune; good for lyrical playing

s2012.d: An Argentinian tango from a collection of seven arranged tangos: sultry, syncopated rhythms and expressive melody ('Little Fireflies'). Needs tango style, accents and rubato.
s2012.rw: Stylish tango; engaging for players and audience

s2015.d: Suzuki's Allegro from Cello Book 1: a bouncy tune with short, separate bow strokes and crisp stops. Develops rhythmic control and bow clarity.

s2017.d: Suzuki's Andantino arranged for cello: a gentle, singing beginner tune. Practises smooth bowing and simple first-position fingerings.
s2017.rw: Simple and pleasing; easy first piece

s2018.d: A short study from Suzuki Cello Book 1, working on string crossings and finger patterns in first position. More technical than tuneful.

s2024.d: A short duet by Hungarian composer Endre Szervánszky for beginner cellists: steady 'tempo giusto' rhythms with folk-like modal colour. Practises ensemble pulse.

s2025.d: Beginner cello piece imitating bagpipes, with a drone-like bass and a folk melody. Practises double-stop drones or open strings and steady rhythm.

s2026.d: Arne's graceful Shakespeare song sung by Ariel in The Tempest (1746): a light, lilting 18th-century melody. Practises clear diction, light tone and neat, simple ornaments.
s2026.rw: Charming tune; good for lyrical playing

s2029.d: Cello arrangement of Bayly's song 'Long, Long Ago' from Suzuki Book 1: a gentle, singing melody that develops legato and simple phrasing.

s2047.d: Suzuki arrangement of Kōjō no Tsuki (Moon over the Ruined Castle): a slow, mournful Japanese melody for cello that builds legato bowing and a singing tone.

s2055.d: Arrangement of Tchaikovsky's piano piece Chanson triste (Op. 40 No. 2, G minor): a plaintive, flowing melody that rewards warm vibrato and expressive shaping.
s2055.rw: Beautiful melody that suits the cello's voice

s2062.d: Rose's cello arrangement of Tchaikovsky's Valse sentimentale: a yearning, elegant F minor waltz with expressive slides, shifts and rubato.
s2062.rw: Much-loved salon piece; great for expression

s2065.d: Arrangement of the famous Garland Waltz from The Sleeping Beauty: sweeping, lilting triple-time melody that needs a generous tone and buoyant rhythm.

s2068.d: Cello arrangement of Tchaikovsky's Chanson triste: a melancholy, lilting minor melody calling for warm tone and expressive shaping.

s2069.d: Tchaikovsky's own arrangement (with Fitzenhagen) of his Nocturne for cello: a tender, songful D minor piece with a rich middle register and expressive high climaxes.

s2071.d: An easy arrangement of the famous horn theme from the slow movement of Symphony No. 5: a broad, yearning melody for developing a singing cello tone.

s2074.d: Arrangement of a Tchaikovsky Neapolitan dance tune: a lively Italianate piece with quickening tempo, crisp rhythms and bounce.

s2075.d: Arrangement of Sweet Reverie (Sweet Dreams) from the Children's Album: a dreamy, flowing melody demanding smooth legato and gentle phrasing.

s2079.d: Arrangement of Telemann's Air Trompette: a bold, fanfare-like Baroque air with bright articulation and trumpet-style figures.

s2097.d: A Telemann scherzo arranged for cello: light, playful Baroque movement with crisp articulation and quick passagework.

s2109.d: A short French educational piece telling a 'little story': lyrical and characterful, with contrasting moods.

s2114.d: A swaying, folky waltz with an Alpine feel; good for triple-time lilt and smooth bowing.

s2115.d: An exotic-sounding minor-key piece evoking an Arabian night; practises atmospheric phrasing and augmented-second colours.

s2117.d: A brisk, fiddle-style piece with lively folk rhythms; practises energetic bowing and clear rhythm.

s2118.d: A gentle, quiet piece evoking footsteps in snow; practises calm, steady bowing and soft tone.

s2119.d: A smooth, flowing beginner piece evoking rolling hills; good for legato bowing and even tone.

s2124.d: A lively, energetic piece with driving rhythms; practises rhythmic drive and confident bowing.

s2126.d: A spacey, playful beginner piece with optional slides evoking a walk on Mars; fun sound effects and simple rhythms.

s2127.d: A light-hearted, quirky cello piece with humorous character; practises rhythm and articulation.

s2128.d: A study-fugue in Baroque style for cello: contrapuntal writing that practises clear voicing and steady rhythm.

s2129.d: A study in the style of Couperin evoking swallows: light, ornamented French Baroque figuration.

s2130.d: An unaccompanied toccata-study for cello: driving, perpetual-motion passagework testing stamina and left-hand agility.

s2131.d: A cheerful, contemporary cello piece with a warm, upbeat character.

s2136.d: A bright, cheerful cello rondo whose catchy theme keeps coming back between contrasting episodes. A long-standing teaching piece for crisp articulation, shifting and a lively bow.

s2140.d: Cello version of the Big Ben chimes tune from Abracadabra. A few notes and even bowing; a gentle first exam piece, with duet or piano part.

s2141.d: A bouncy Northumbrian nursery tune in a lilting compound rhythm. Practises a light, rocking bow stroke and steady pulse.

s2144.d: Suzuki Cello Book 1 setting of 'Go Tell Aunt Rhody'. A plain, singing tune for even bows and accurate first-position fingers.

s2146.d: The Tudor ballad 'Greensleeves' as a duet: a wistful minor-key melody in flowing triple time. Needs smooth legato and good ensemble with the partner.

s2170.d: A short Provençal folk melody as a cello duet from the Second-Year Method. Practises legato phrasing and ensemble playing.

s2171.d: The nursery song 'The Noble Duke of York' as a cello duet. A marching tune for firm rhythm and steady bowing.

s2172.d: A gospel-style spiritual tune from Team Strings for beginner cello. Simple, rhythmic and repetitive, practising steady bowing.

s2173.d: Rebecca Clarke's arrangement of an old Scottish/Borders air, a slow, tender melody with a rich piano part. Needs a beautiful tone, control at slow tempo and subtle phrasing.

s2177.d: The Shaker tune 'Simple Gifts' (known from Copland's Appalachian Spring), unaccompanied for cello. Practises clean intonation and a calm, singing tone.

s2178.d: The English ballad 'Scarborough Fair', a haunting Dorian-mode melody in triple time. Practises legato and expressive phrasing.
s2178.rw: Haunting melody; easy to play musically

s2189.d: 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star' for beginner cello, top line alone or as a duet. Practises even bowing and simple first-position fingers.

s2192.d: A short Argentine folk melody for cello with a gentle Latin lilt. Practises lyrical bowing and rhythmic feel.

s2193.d: The Yiddish folk song 'Tumbalalaika', a minor-key waltz. Practises lilting triple time and expressive, slightly melancholy phrasing.

s2194.d: A playful, bouncy tune from Vamoosh Book 2. Practises detached bowing and character.

s2197.d: 'Old MacDonald Had a Farm' for beginner cello from Cello Basics. Cheerful and simple, for steady rhythm and bowing.

s2198.d: A gentle folk-style melody in a Harrison arrangement for cello. Practises lyrical tone and shaping.

s2199.d: The French children's song 'J'ai du bon tabac'. A jaunty, simple tune for clear rhythm and even articulation.

s2202.d: Choice of Irish/Northumbrian tunes: the lyrical 'Danny Boy', the brisk 'Star of the County Down' or the dancing 'The Keel Row'. Practises either singing tone or folk rhythm.

s2205.d: 'Parson's Farewell', an English country dance from Playford's Dancing Master (1651), with a stately minor-key opening and quicker section. Practises rhythm and contrast.

s2207.d: The 'Skye Boat Song', a lilting Scottish boat song in 6/8. Practises smooth legato, steady rocking rhythm and gentle phrasing.

s2217.d: Sheku Kanneh-Mason's unaccompanied setting of the Northumbrian song 'Blow the Wind Southerly'. Lyrical and spacious, using chords and higher positions to create a full sound alone.

s2218.d: Sheku Kanneh-Mason's unaccompanied arrangement of the Irish tune 'Star of the County Down'. Rhythmic and folk-like with chords and double stops for a full texture.

s2224.d: Two unaccompanied Shetland/Scottish session tunes for cello: a lively dance and a reel. Practises folk bowing and rhythmic independence.

s2225.d: The American 'Saratoga Hornpipe', unaccompanied for cello. Dotted hornpipe rhythm with quick string crossings and a driving pulse.

s2226.d: The Irish jig 'Snug in a Blanket', unaccompanied for cello. Lilting 6/8 rhythm practising bow control and pulse.

s2227.d: Choice of two unaccompanied session tunes for cello: the Irish reel 'The Pigeon on the Gate' or 'The Reconciliation'. Practises folk rhythm and bow independence.

s2228.d: Two traditional hornpipes for cello in a Nelson arrangement, with dotted rhythms and quick string crossings. Practises rhythmic drive and agility.

s2229.d: 'Au clair de la lune' as a cello duet. Simple French tune for even bowing and ensemble.

s2235.d: Arrangement of the old English singing-game tune 'Jenny Jones'. A simple, rocking melody suited to practising smooth bowing and accurate finger patterns.

s2236.d: Arrangement of the well-known Scottish song with its broad, swinging melody. Practises a warm, sustained tone, the Scotch-snap rhythm and shaping a phrase.

s2238.d: Arrangement of a gentle traditional Czech (Moravian) carol in a slow, rocking style. Practises steady, smooth bowing and good intonation in a first-position melody.

s2239.d: Arrangement of the English nursery rhyme 'Pease Pudding Hot'. A short, perky tune practising clear rhythm, crisp bow changes and simple finger patterns.
s2239.rw: Bright and simple; easy to secure

s2240.d: Duet arrangement of the gentle Czech carol 'Rocking' ('Little Jesus, sweetly sleep'). A slow lullaby that practises smooth legato and keeping together with a partner.

s2242.d: A short traditional tune arranged for beginner cellists in the Abracadabra Cello book. A simple melody for practising basic finger placement and even bowing.

s2243.d: The familiar American folk song from Suzuki Book 1. A simple, steady melody in first position practising even bow strokes and finger patterns.

s2250.d: Arrangement of the Chinese folk song 'Mo Li Hua' (Jasmine Flower). A graceful pentatonic melody practising smooth legato and a delicate, singing tone.
s2250.rw: Elegant tune; shows a lovely tone

s2256.d: Joachim Stutschewsky's cello setting of a Jewish/Israeli folk melody. A songful, modal piece with an expressive, yearning character, calling for rich tone and flexible phrasing.

s2257.d: The simple French folk tune from Suzuki Cello Book 1. Practises string crossings, finger patterns and an even, relaxed bow.
s2257.rw: Familiar Suzuki piece; easy to secure

s2259.d: Duet arrangements of two famous tunes: the English 'Greensleeves' or the Scottish 'Skye Boat Song'. Both are flowing, lyrical melodies practising tone and keeping in time with a partner.
s2259.rw: Lovely familiar tunes; good ensemble work

s2267.d: An Irish traditional tune from The Enchanted Isle, arranged for cello. Expect a light, flowing melody suited to practising tone and phrasing.

s2285.d: Arrangement of the Northumbrian folk song made famous by Kathleen Ferrier. A broad, lyrical melody calling for warm, singing tone and long phrases.

s2286.d: Arrangement of the lively Northumbrian song and dance tune 'The Keel Row'. At this grade likely treated with variations, demanding agile fingers, bow control and rhythmic spring.

s2287.d: A short Irish air arranged for beginner cellists. A simple, songful melody practising smooth legato and tone.

s2288.d: Arrangement of the French carol tune 'Noël nouvelet', known as the Easter hymn 'Now the Green Blade Riseth'. A modal, flowing minor melody practising tone and steady bowing.

s2289.d: Arrangement of the Yiddish folk song 'Tumbalalaika'. A wistful minor-key waltz-like tune practising lilting 3/4 phrasing and tone.

s2290.d: Arrangement of the Welsh lullaby 'Ar Hyd y Nos'. A calm, flowing melody in a gentle rocking rhythm, practising smooth legato, long phrases and a warm tone.

s2291.d: Arrangement of the American folk song 'She'll Be Coming Round the Mountain'. A jaunty, upbeat tune practising rhythm and clear bow strokes.

s2295.d: Arrangement of a Congolese call-and-response children's song. Cheerful and rhythmic with syncopation, practising rhythmic precision and bright bowing.

s2297.d: Arrangement of a Czech folk dance by Kathy and David Blackwell. A sturdy, stamping dance with a strong beat, practising firm, rhythmic bowing.

s0949.d: An unaccompanied cello piece in American fiddle/folk style: lively rhythms and double stops in a solo setting.

x00971.d: Ligeti's solo cello sonata in two movements: a lyrical Dialogo and a fiery Capriccio. Tests tone, double stops and virtuosity.

x00973.d: Cello arrangement of Stravinsky's Pulcinella suite, witty and neoclassical in five movements. Tests rhythm and character.

x00974.d: Turnage's rhythmic, jazz-influenced piece for cello with energetic lines and lyrical moments. Tests rhythm and stamina.

x00975.d: Zimmermann's four short studies for solo cello with sharp, angular modern writing. Tests extended techniques and rhythm.

x01057.d: Paganini's variations on a theme from Rossini's Mosè in Egitto, played on a single string. Tests agility, harmonics and left-hand stretches.

x02007.d: Classical cello sonata with graceful singing lines and bright finale; practises clean intonation and Classical style.

x02008.d: Variations on a Finnish folk song ('Little Golden One') for cello and piano; lyrical and romantic with varied moods.

x02009.d: Italian Baroque sonata with slow-fast movements; practises ornamentation, clean bowing and stylish continuo interplay.

x02010.d: Theme and variations on 'La ci darem la mano' from Mozart's Don Giovanni; showy, practises agility and lyrical charm.

x02011.d: Compact three-movement sonata of 1915 with Pierrot-like wit and Spanish touches; practises colour, rubato and extended techniques.

x02012.d: Slow, hushed movement from the Quatuor pour la fin du temps; sustained cello line over steady piano chords, testing control and breath of bow.

x02013.d: Strong, tautly written mid-century British sonata; practises dramatic projection and rhythmic drive.

x02014.d: Georgian folk-based short pieces for cello and piano; practises dance rhythms, harmonics and expressive colour.

x03119.d: Finishing movements of Boccherini's B-flat concerto (Grützmacher version): a songful Adagio and a bright rondo finale with rapid passagework and wide leaps.

x03121.d: Cassadó's three-movement solo suite: Preludio-Fantasia, Sardana and Intermezzo e danza finale. Spanish flavour, double stops, harmonics and technical bravura throughout.

x03122.d: Seven folk-inspired movements by Bright Sheng, from Chinese tunes: evocative, with plucked and glissando effects, rhythmic drive and song-like melodies. A varied, colourful cello cycle.

y00012.d: Prélude from Bach's Cello Suite No. 4 in E♭: a flowing, arpeggio-based movement spanning wide range, practising string crossings, intonation and long-line shaping.

y00013.d: Beethoven's seven variations on 'Bei Männern' from The Magic Flute: elegant, graceful variations practising Classical phrasing, clean passagework and expressive tone.

y00322.d: Brahms's Cello Sonata No. 1 in E minor, Op. 38 (1865). Deep Romantic writing with a fugal finale.

y00323.d: Grieg's Cello Sonata in A minor, Op. 36 (1883). Passionate, folk-tinged Romantic sonata.

y00324.d: Schumann's Three Fantasy Pieces, Op. 73 (1849), originally for clarinet. Warm and lyrical, with fast, passionate last movement.

y00490.d: Rondo (Allegro) finale of Beethoven's Cello Sonata in G minor, Op. 5 No. 2 (1796). Bright, playful with quick runs.

y00495.d: Tchaikovsky's Variations on a Rococo Theme, Op. 33 (1876), original version ed. Wallfisch or Fitzenhagen's. Elegant, brilliant theme and variations.

z00459.d: Fast, lively final movement of Beethoven's G minor cello sonata, a rondo with sparkling passages. Practises quick passagework, agility and Classical wit.

z00466.d: Allegro from a Baroque sonata by Cervetto. Practises brisk bowing, clear passagework and Baroque style.

z00467.d: Lively Scherzo from Chopin's G minor cello sonata, with dance-like energy. Practises quick figuration, rhythmic drive and light bowing.

z00468.d: Intermezzo from Lalo's Cello Concerto, alternating a gentle Spanish-flavoured tune with a lively, dance-like section. Practises rhythmic contrast, lyrical phrasing and agile passagework.

z00469.d: First movement of Monn's G minor concerto, with strong rhythms and quick passages. Practises rhythmic drive, wide leaps and clear Baroque-Classical style.

z00470.d: Fiery movement from Schumann's Fantasiestücke with fast, forceful passagework. Practises rhythmic drive, tone projection and quick passages.

z00471.d: Famous flowing Prélude from Bach's first cello suite, played unaccompanied. Practises smooth string crossing, steady pulse and shaping of harmony.

z00472.d: Short, deeply felt Adagio from Elgar's Cello Concerto, a long singing line full of yearning. Practises expressive tone, vibrato and sustained phrasing.

z00473.d: Andante molto tranquillo from Grieg's A minor cello sonata, a gentle, lyrical movement. Practises sustained tone, Romantic phrasing and balance with piano.

z00474.d: Adagio from Haydn's D major cello concerto, a graceful and noble Classical melody. Practises sustained singing tone, clean shifting and refined Classical style.

z00475.d: Slow movement of Monn's G minor concerto, a gentle expressive Baroque-Classical song. Practises sustained tone, phrasing and ornamentation.

z00476.d: Andante from Rachmaninov's G minor cello sonata, a passionate, flowing Romantic movement. Practises rich tone, long phrases and wide expressive shaping.

z00477.d: Preludio and Allemanda from Vivaldi's G minor sonata. Practises sustained opening phrasing and clear, stylish Baroque dance movement.

Pütz: Luxembourg composer of wind band and educational music with jazz and pop influences.
Williams, arr. Galliford: Film composer of Star Wars, Indiana Jones, Harry Potter and Schindler's List.
Szokolay: Hungarian composer best known for his opera Blood Wedding.
L. Berkeley: English composer, pupil of Nadia Boulanger, writing in a refined, neoclassical style influenced by French music.
Elgar: Leading English late-Romantic composer of the Enigma Variations and the violin and cello concertos.
Corrette: French organist, composer and author of many instrumental tutors.
Diabelli: Viennese publisher and composer of much teaching music, remembered for the waltz on which Beethoven wrote his Diabelli Variations.
Cheney: Composer of educational cello pieces; details uncertain.
Lully, arr. Lengyel: Court composer to Louis XIV, father of French opera.
Grieg: Norway's leading Romantic composer, famed for folk-inspired melody and the Piano Concerto.
Gilbert & Ory, arr. Harrison: American jazz trombonist and composer of Muskrat Ramble.
Trad., arr. Sassmannshaus: Authors of the Early Start and Recital Album string series for young players (Bärenreiter).
Sollima: Sicilian cellist-composer blending classical, folk, rock and minimalist influences.
De Fesch: Dutch Baroque violinist and composer active in Antwerp and London.
